findings.summary: INV-8 guarantees no file is ever both `unmodeled` and paired, but `unmodeled_markdown` never consults `config["pairs"]`, so a doc explicitly declared in a pair's `docs` glob is still reported as unmodeled.
findings.evidence: Doc INV-8: "Every path in `unmodeled` sits in a directory holding no candidate code file, so no file is ever both unmodeled and paired." Doc §2 defines Pair as "`{label, code[], docs[]}` — links code globs to spec doc(s)." Code (`unmodeled_markdown`) filters on only three conditions: `if d in code_dirs: continue`, `if classify_exclude(md, user_excludes) == "user": continue`, `if os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(md))[0].lower() in CONVENTIONAL_DOC_STEMS: continue` — no `pair_docs` check, unlike orphan detection which does have `if md in pair_docs: continue  # explicitly paired — governed, wherever its code is`.
findings.suggestion: Pass the computed `pair_docs` set into `unmodeled_markdown` and skip any md in it (mirroring the orphan rule), or reword INV-8 to claim only same-stem pairing ("no file is ever both unmodeled and co-located-paired").

verification.doc_quote: | INV-8 | Every path in `unmodeled` sits in a directory holding no candidate code file, so no file is ever both unmodeled and paired. |
verification.why: The cited invariant line itself carries the full guarantee ("no file is ever both unmodeled and paired"), and no other passage states that pairing guarantee correctly — §3's three-condition list neither makes nor corrects the pairing claim, so the document does assert it as written.

findings.summary: The Definitions table says a markdown file is unmodeled when it has "no code sibling", but the code's actual test is that its whole directory holds no candidate code file.
findings.evidence: Doc §2: "UNMODELED | A directory tree of at least 3 markdown files that same-stem pairing cannot reach — no code sibling, not a conventional doc." Code: `code_dirs = {os.path.dirname(rel) for rel in candidate}` … `if d in code_dirs: continue  # sits beside code — the pairing model already sees it`. So `src/notes-a.md`, `src/notes-b.md`, `src/notes-c.md` next to a single `src/app.py` have no code siblings yet are never reported as unmodeled. (Doc §3 states the directory-level rule correctly.)
findings.suggestion: Change the §2 row to match §3: "…sits in a directory holding no candidate code file, and is not a conventional doc."

verification.doc_quote: A file qualifies when it sits in a directory holding no candidate code, is not user-excluded, and is not a conventional doc name.
verification.why: §3 "Unmodeled markdown detection" states the directory-level rule correctly; the Definitions-table gloss "no code sibling" is the loose shorthand of the same rule, so the document is not wrong.
